headline: Philadelphia, Galaxy, Whitecaps, Nashville all take road points
dek: Fourteen matches across Sept. 18-20 produced one goalless draw, four thrillers above three goals each, and no shortage of away-side damage.
body: Red Bull New York edged New York City FC 1-0 on Sept. 18. Columbus rolled into Montreal and won 2-0 a day later, while Charlotte FC beat D.C. United 2-1 and Orlando fell 4-2 at New England. San Jose and LAFC split 2-2. On Sept. 20, Philadelphia Union won 4-3 at Sporting Kansas City, LA Galaxy took Minnesota 3-2, Nashville blanked Chicago 3-0, Vancouver claimed a 3-0 away win at Real Salt Lake, Atlanta United won 1-0 at Portland, and St. Louis beat Toronto 3-1. Colorado and Seattle drew 3-3. FC Dallas and Austin FC finished 0-0.

headline: Kelsy to Rangers, Kerr to Portugal, Ngando released
dek: Three players exit MLS as one confirmed arrival reshapes Charlotte FC's books.
body: Portland Timbers forward Kevin Kelsy, who logged 1,500 minutes this season, has transferred to Rangers FC in Scotland. Toronto FC forward Deandre Kerr, 780 minutes in 2026, moves to AVS Futebol SAD in Portugal's second division. Vancouver Whitecaps midfielder J.C. Ngando, 1,140 minutes this season, had his contract mutually terminated on Sept. 3 and has cleared waivers. On the incoming side, defender JahLane Forbes has joined Charlotte FC.

headline: Musa holds three-goal cushion with table crunch looming
dek: FC Dallas's Petar Musa leads at 18 goals while a two-man pack sits three back with the standings tightening.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the individual scoring race with 18 goals. Sam Surridge of Nashville SC and Nicolás Fernández of New York City FC share second at 15 apiece. In the assists column, Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC leads on 10, with Evander of FC Cincinnati and Son Heung-Min of LAFC tied at 9. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver has compiled a league-high 100 tackles, 28 clear of Yannick Bright of Inter Miami CF on 72 and Silvan Hefti of D.C. United on 61.

headline: Guilherme and Fernández beat the model; Almirón and Son trail it badly
dek: Two strikers are converting at nearly double their expected rate; two others owe the xG ledger a combined 9.7 goals.
body: Guilherme of Houston Dynamo FC leads xG overperformance: 13 goals against an xG of 6.4, a gap of plus-6.6. Nicolás Fernández of New York City FC matches that margin exactly, 15 goals, xG 8.4, plus-6.6. At the other end, Miguel Almirón of Atlanta United has scored just 4 goals against an xG of 8.9, a deficit of 4.9. Son Heung-Min of LAFC has 5 goals against an xG of 9.8, trailing expectation by 4.8.

headline: Philadelphia rout San Diego 5-0; Red Bulls take Hudson derby
dek: Four results across the week produced 11 goals, one shutout, and no home wins.
body: New England took the points at Chicago on Sept. 13, winning 2-1, while Austin FC claimed a 2-1 road result in Vancouver the same day. San Diego's home fixture on Sept. 14 turned into a rout: Philadelphia Union won 5-0 at San Diego FC, the heaviest scoreline of the week. The Hudson River derby closed the round on Sept. 18, Red Bull New York beating New York City FC 1-0 on the road at Yankee Stadium.

headline: Three exits, two arrivals as transfer window reshapes rosters
dek: LAFC, San Diego, and Colorado all lose players to Europe; Galaxy and Toronto add depth.
body: David Martínez departed LAFC for FC Midtjylland of the Danish Superliga, having logged 1,290 minutes this season. Luca Bombino left San Diego FC for Stoke City of the EFL Championship, also on 1,290 minutes. Lucas Herrington ended his Colorado Rapids season at 1,650 minutes before transferring to Premier League side Hull City. On the incoming side, LA Galaxy acquired defender Lucas Calegari from Turkish Süper Lig club Eyüpspor. Toronto FC signed Colombian winger Alejandro Piedrahita on loan from Bulgarian first-division club CSKA Sofia.

headline: Musa leads at 18; Fernández and Surridge tied at 15
dek: FC Dallas striker holds a three-goal cushion with the season entering its final stretch.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas sits atop the scoring charts with 18 goals. Nashville SC's Sam Surridge and New York City FC's Nicolás Fernández are level in second at 15. In assists, San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer leads with 10, one clear of a two-way tie at nine between Evander of FC Cincinnati and Son Heung-Min of LAFC. In the tackle count, Vancouver Whitecaps midfielder Andrés Cubas has reached 100, well ahead of Yannick Bright of Inter Miami CF at 72 and D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 61.

headline: Guilherme and Fernández finish chances; Almirón and Son owe the model
dek: Two strikers are banking goals at nearly double expected rate; two others are well short of their xG.
body: Houston Dynamo FC's Guilherme leads the overperformers with 13 goals against an xG of 6.4, a gap of plus-6.6. Nicolás Fernández of NYCFC matches that differential exactly, 15 goals, xG of 8.4. At the other end, Atlanta United FC's Miguel Almirón has scored four goals against an xG of 8.9, a shortfall of 4.9. LAFC's Son Heung-Min has five goals on an xG of 9.8, running 4.8 goals below model. Nashville SC lead the East at 54 points on a 16-6-3 record; Vancouver Whitecaps front the West at 46 on 14-4-6. Inter Miami CF boast the league's best attack with 61 goals; Nashville hold the best defense at 21 conceded.

headline: Fourteen games, one blank scoresheet in busy MLS weekend
dek: Goals flew across both conferences Sept. 12-14, with Philadelphia Union the week's loudest statement-makers.
body: Philadelphia Union silenced San Diego FC 5-0 on Sept. 14 to stand out in a packed fixture window. Orlando City put three past Toronto FC. St. Louis CITY SC beat Minnesota United 4-2, and Sporting Kansas City downed LAFC 3-1. FC Cincinnati and Charlotte FC traded three goals apiece at TQL Stadium. Inter Miami and Nashville split four goals in a 2-2 draw. New England Revolution won 2-1 at Chicago, Austin FC edged Vancouver 2-1, and NYCFC claimed all three points at Real Salt Lake 2-0. D.C. United and Atlanta United played out the round's lone 0-0.

headline: Houston lose two, San Diego add World Cup striker
dek: The Houston Dynamo's defensive and midfield core has thinned significantly, while San Diego FC bolster their attack with veteran firepower and youth.
body: Houston Dynamo FC shed two first-team regulars before the transfer window closed. Defender Erik Sviatchenko, 1,530 minutes into the 2026 season, departed for Thai top-flight side Port FC. Midfielder Jack McGlynn, 1,500 minutes in, was transferred to EFL Championship club Stoke City. At FC Cincinnati, defender Matt Miazga was waived after logging 1,140 minutes this season. On the arrivals side, San Diego FC signed striker Cédric Bakambu as a free agent following his spell with Real Betis, and added 18-year-old Cameroonian midfielder David Mimbang on loan from sister club FC Nordsjælland.

headline: Musa leads at 18; Surridge and Fernández share second
dek: FC Dallas's striker holds a three-goal cushion over two players tied at 15 with the season entering its final stretch.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads MLS in goals with 18, three clear of Sam Surridge (Nashville SC) and Nicolás Fernández (New York City FC), who sit level at 15. In the assists race, Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC fronts the field with 10, one ahead of Evander (FC Cincinnati) and Son Heung-Min (LAFC) at nine apiece. In xG variance, Guilherme of Houston Dynamo and Fernández are the league's biggest overperformers, each netting 6.6 goals above expectation. Miguel Almirón (Atlanta United) and Son Heung-Min sit deepest below their xG marks, at -4.9 and -4.8 respectively.

headline: Nashville lead East at 54 pts; Vancouver front the West
dek: The Eastern frontrunner doubles as the league's stingiest defense, while the West stays close behind.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference with 54 points on a 16W-6D-3L record, having conceded just 21 goals, the fewest in MLS, while scoring 50. In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps sit first with 46 points at 14W-4D-6L. Inter Miami CF own the league's most productive attack at 61 goals scored, nine more than any other side has managed against the backdrop of a 53-goal Western frontrunner. Nashville's defensive ledger at 21 allowed doubles as both a conference and league benchmark.
